hints: Focus on what holds the $\text{N}_2\text{F}_4$ molecule together and which bond is weakest and most likely to break first on heating.
Draw $\text{F}_2\text{N}-\text{NF}_2$ and see that breaking the central bond gives two identical fragments, so X must be $\text{NF}_2$.
Consider the bond enthalpy of the bond you break for the $\Delta H$ value, then count electron domains around N in X to decide its shape.
walkthrough:
**Identify product X**

Think of $\text{N}_2\text{F}_4$ as $\text{F}_2\text{N}-\text{NF}_2$. Heating breaks the weakest bond.

The N-N single bond is much weaker than N-F, so it breaks:
$$\text{N}_2\text{F}_4 \rightarrow 2\text{NF}_2$$
So the single product X is $\text{NF}_2$.

**Check statement 1**

Only the N-N bond is broken to make X. No N-F bonds are broken.

So statement 1 is incorrect.

**Check statement 2 using bond enthalpy**

Enthalpy change is approximately the energy needed to break the bonds broken.

$$\Delta H \approx +E(\text{N-N})$$
The N-N single bond enthalpy is about $+160 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, so $\Delta H \approx +160 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$. So statement 2 is correct.

**Check statement 3 using shape of X**

In $\text{NF}_2$, N forms 2 sigma bonds to F and has a lone pair plus an unpaired electron.

With 2 bonding domains and lone pairs, repulsion bends the molecule, just like in $\text{NO}_2$. It cannot be linear. So statement 3 is correct.

**Combine the conclusions**

Statements 2 and 3 are correct, but 1 is not.

This corresponds to the 2 and 3 only combination.

options.A: Incorrect. This would mean 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Statement 1 is wrong because only the N-N bond breaks to give $2\text{NF}_2$, the four N-F bonds remain intact.
options.B: Incorrect. This would mean 1 and 2 only are correct. Statement 1 is wrong for the same reason, and it misses that statement 3 is correct because $\text{NF}_2$ is bent and non-linear.
options.C: Correct. Statement 2 is right because $\Delta H$ is about $+E(\text{N-N}) \approx +160 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, and statement 3 is right because $\text{NF}_2$ has lone pair repulsion and is bent, while statement 1 is wrong.
options.D: Incorrect. This would mean only statement 1 is correct. In fact statement 1 is the only false statement, since N-F bonds are not broken, only the central N-N bond is broken.
